blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Queen Mary Park the park sits at 8972 Queen Mary Boulevard, north of 88 Avenue and west of 132 Street, and the City lists it under Whalley and City Centre.

The house area takes its name from that park and Queen Mary Boulevard: its east side reaches King George Boulevard and Bear Creek Park at 13750 88 Avenue, and its west side reaches Scott Road (120 Street).
Bear Creek Park, at the area's northeast at 13750 88 Avenue, is a separate, larger City park — not part of Queen Mary Park itself.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Detached houses here surround a park that is mostly natural area, not playing fields: the City states the majority of Queen Mary Park is natural areas established to protect Healy Creek, with trails and a playground reached from the trails.

Kennedy Trail Elementary, at 8305 122A Street at the area's southwest, is the school the Kennedy Trail name in local complex names comes from — the elementary itself is a School District 36 school, confirmed on its district page.
The area's detached stock sits between two RapidBus corridors, King George Boulevard to the east and Scott Road to the west, rather than around a single village centre.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Healy Creek is the rule that matters most on park-edge lots: Queen Mary Park's natural areas were established to protect the sensitive ecosystem of Healy Creek, an important tributary to Bear Creek and the Serpentine River, so a lot backing onto the park or the creek needs a riparian check in the City mapping before a rebuild is assumed.

For the city-wide Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH), suite and Zoning By-law No. 12000 position, see the Surrey houses-for-sale guide; the Queen Mary Park-specific point is the Healy Creek / Bear Creek riparian setting above, not a separate neighbourhood zone.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Queen Mary Park is open dawn until dusk, at 8972 Queen Mary Boulevard, with park contact 604-501-5050 — the park has no sports-field lighting or evening facility use stated on its City page.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Houses: getting around

items.t: The R6 Scott Road RapidBus connects Scott Road Station to Newton Exchange along Scott Road and 72 Avenue, serving the area's west edge at 120 Street.

The R1 King George Boulevard RapidBus connects Newton Exchange to Guildford Exchange along King George Boulevard, serving the area's east edge, and RapidBus routes run at least every 10 minutes at peak and every 15 minutes off-peak, 6 a.m. to midnight.
The nearest SkyTrain stations are on King George Boulevard at Surrey Central and King George stations, reached via the R1 — no SkyTrain station sits inside Queen Mary Park itself.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check any lot touching Healy Creek or Bear Creek against the City's riparian and flood mapping: Queen Mary Park's natural areas protect Healy Creek as a tributary to Bear Creek and the Serpentine River, and the park page does not state the setback or flood status of any private lot.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Queen Mary Park?
faq.a: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board counted 66 houses listed in Queen Mary Park at the end of October 2026. The number changes daily, so ask Jared for today’s count.

faq.q: Is Queen Mary Park a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: Queen Mary Park houses sold at a sales ratio of 3% in October 2026, a buyers’ market on the reports’ scale (under 12% favours buyers, over 20% favours sellers).

faq.q: How many houses sold in Queen Mary Park from June to October 2026?
faq.a: Between June and October 2026, 15 houses sold in Queen Mary Park; Surrey as a whole recorded 464.

faq.q: Which elementary school serves Queen Mary Park houses?
faq.a: Kennedy Trail Elementary is the area's named elementary, at 8305 122A Street, and the district page confirms it as a School District 36 school with phone 604-590-1198.

faq.q: What is inside Queen Mary Park itself?
faq.a: Mostly protected natural area. Natural trails loop through the northwest portion, entered from Queen Mary Boulevard at 130B Street and from the end of Lanark Place, with a playground in the middle reached from the trails.

faq.q: How close is Bear Creek Park?
faq.a: Bear Creek Park is at 13750 88 Avenue, at the northeast of this house area across King George Boulevard from the Queen Mary Boulevard streets. It is a separate City park from Queen Mary Park at 8972 Queen Mary Boulevard, so a listing that names both parks is naming two different parks on opposite sides of the area.

faq.q: Does this area have RapidBus on both sides?
faq.a: Yes, on its two edges. The R6 Scott Road RapidBus runs on Scott Road (120 Street) on the west side, from Scott Road Station to Newton Exchange, and the R1 King George Boulevard RapidBus runs on King George Boulevard on the east side, from Newton Exchange to Guildford Exchange. Neither route runs through the interior Queen Mary Boulevard streets.

faq.q: What did houses in Queen Mary Park sell for?
faq.a: The median house sale in Queen Mary Park was $1,178,500, across 43 sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Queen Mary Park?
faq.a: The median was 28 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 95.3% of the last list price (7% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
